purpose: Use one substantive participant-facing question per response field. Six domains remain for navigation, while each field targets one construct or bounded context question. This prevents checklist prompts from being collapsed into a single answer box.

RRQ_TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT.title: Relationship timeline & context
RRQ_TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT.intro: Start with what actually happened. Short answers are fine when the fact is simple.

fields.label: What was the romantic timeline of the relationship?
fields.placeholder: When it became romantic, roughly how long that lasted, and what the relationship is now.
fields.clarification_prompt: If there were distinct phases, name them separately.

fields.label: How much were you actually together physically?
fields.placeholder: Cohabitation, frequent in-person time, long-distance, or prolonged separation.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say what was different when together versus apart, if anything.

fields.label: Which major transitions or constraints materially affected the relationship?
fields.placeholder: Breakups/reunions, marriage, other partners, religion, family, health, money, immigration, language, or sexual opportunity.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name the constraint or transition and the phase it affected.

RRQ_LOVE_EROS_DIRECTION.title: Love, attraction & being in love
RRQ_LOVE_EROS_DIRECTION.intro: Answer each direction separately. Attraction, love, being in love, and commitment are different constructs.

fields.label: How physically attracted were you to them?
fields.placeholder: Focus only on physical attraction, not whether the sex was good or whether you loved them.
fields.clarification_prompt: If attraction changed, say when.

fields.label: How romantically in love were you with them?
fields.placeholder: Think longing, romantic specialness, reciprocity, and romantic priority—not merely caring deeply.
fields.clarification_prompt: If love and being in love differed, say how.

fields.label: How much did you love or feel attached to them?
fields.placeholder: This can stay high even when romantic Eros or sexual desire is low.
fields.clarification_prompt: If attachment changed, say when.

fields.label: How much did you want a durable partnership or marriage with them?
fields.placeholder: Answer what you wanted, not whether the relationship was practically workable.
fields.clarification_prompt: If your commitment intent changed, say why.

fields.label: As best you could tell, how physically attracted were they to you?
fields.placeholder: Use direct statements or behavior when possible; mark unknown if you truly cannot tell.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate evidence from inference if needed.

fields.label: As best you could tell, how romantically in love were they with you?
fields.placeholder: Do not substitute love, sex, jealousy, or marriage intent for being in love.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say what evidence makes you think this.

fields.label: As best you could tell, how much did they love or feel attached to you?
fields.placeholder: Use direct statements or behavior when possible.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate what you know from what you infer.

fields.label: As best you could tell, how much did they want a durable partnership or marriage with you?
fields.placeholder: Commitment intent is separate from love or practical fit.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say what evidence makes you think this.

RRQ_SEXUAL_SYSTEM.title: Sexual system
RRQ_SEXUAL_SYSTEM.intro: Keep general libido, desire for this specific partner, satisfaction, and chemistry separate.

fields.label: What was your general libido like during this period?
fields.placeholder: Think sexual appetite across contexts, not just desire for this partner.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate general libido from partner-specific desire.

fields.label: How strongly did you specifically want this partner sexually?
fields.placeholder: This can differ from your general libido.
fields.clarification_prompt: If it changed with familiarity or distance, say so.

fields.label: As best you could tell, what was their general libido like?
fields.placeholder: Do not infer low libido from religion, virginity, health, distance, or lack of opportunity.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say what evidence exists and what remains unknown.

fields.label: As best you could tell, how strongly did they specifically want you sexually?
fields.placeholder: Separate partner-specific desire from their general libido.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say what evidence exists and what remains inference.

fields.label: When sexual contact happened, how satisfying was it for you?
fields.placeholder: Focus on your actual experience, not attraction alone.
fields.clarification_prompt: If satisfaction varied, describe the condition.

fields.label: As best you could tell, how satisfying was sexual contact for them?
fields.placeholder: Use direct feedback or behavior; mark unknown if you cannot tell.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate evidence from inference.

fields.label: How well did your sexual systems fit together as a pair?
fields.placeholder: Think responsiveness, desire match, ease, and actual interaction—not attraction alone.
fields.clarification_prompt: If chemistry and attraction differed, say how.

fields.label: Did either person's sexual desire change as familiarity increased or after time apart/reunion?
fields.placeholder: Name whose desire changed and the time course.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate partner-specific decline from general libido.

fields.label: What, if anything, limited what sexual behavior could reveal about desire?
fields.placeholder: Religion, virginity, health, distance, opportunity, relationship rules, trauma, or other constraints.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say which person's behavior was constrained and how.

RRQ_MIND_COMMUNICATION.title: Mind & communication
RRQ_MIND_COMMUNICATION.intro: Reasoning fit, stimulation, communication amount, shared interests, and spiritual connection are separate.

fields.label: How well could the two of you reason together?
fields.placeholder: Think productive disagreement, mutual comprehension, and building ideas together.
fields.clarification_prompt: Give an interaction example if the answer is not obvious.

fields.label: How well did they understand and apply difficult ideas you discussed?
fields.placeholder: Do not use education, occupation, language fluency, or talkativeness as substitutes.
fields.clarification_prompt: Give an observed example if possible.

fields.label: How much did they genuinely expand or change your thinking?
fields.placeholder: This is different from simply having good conversations or being intelligent.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name something genuinely new or mind-expanding if there was any.

fields.label: How good was the quality of communication between you?
fields.placeholder: Think clarity, honesty, mutual understanding, and ability to discuss difficult things.
fields.clarification_prompt: Do not answer only with how often you talked.

fields.label: How much meaningful communication did you actually have?
fields.placeholder: Focus on amount and continuity, not quality.
fields.clarification_prompt: If it changed by phase, say when.

fields.label: How much meaningful common ground did you have in interests, activities, or worldview?
fields.placeholder: Shared interests are separate from communication quality.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name a few examples if useful.

fields.label: How much useful knowledge did they contribute that you lacked?
fields.placeholder: This can be high without being globally mind-expanding.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name the domains where this mattered.

fields.label: How relevant were spirituality, religion, intuition, mystical experience, or metaphysical ideas in this relationship?
fields.placeholder: If relevant, distinguish experiencing it from being curious about it or stimulating each other's thinking.
fields.clarification_prompt: Say what kind of spiritual/mystical connection existed, if any.

RRQ_EMOTIONAL_AUTONOMY.title: Emotional climate & autonomy
RRQ_EMOTIONAL_AUTONOMY.intro: Keep intimacy, readability, responsiveness, drama, serious conflict, repair, autonomy, and jealousy separate.

fields.label: How safe and natural did confiding or deep disclosure feel with this partner?
fields.placeholder: Focus on psychological intimacy, not simply love or time spent together.
fields.clarification_prompt: If one direction differed, say so.

fields.label: How easy was it for you to tell what they were really feeling or thinking?
fields.placeholder: A caring partner can still be hard to read.
fields.clarification_prompt: Mark unknown if their internal state was often opaque.

fields.label: How understood, validated, and appropriately responded to did you feel?
fields.placeholder: Focus on how they responded to your needs and inner experience.
fields.clarification_prompt: Give an example if the answer is mixed.

fields.label: How much expressive, theatrical, playful, or demonstrative drama was there?
fields.placeholder: Do not count serious hostility here unless it was also theatrical.
fields.clarification_prompt: Clarify whether the drama was enjoyable, tiring, or neutral if relevant.

fields.label: How much genuinely serious conflict, hostility, contempt, coercion, or aggression was there?
fields.placeholder: Keep this separate from playful or theatrical drama.
fields.clarification_prompt: If there were rare severe episodes, distinguish frequency from severity.

fields.label: When conflict happened, how difficult was it to repair and reconnect?
fields.placeholder: Think time, effort, apology, understanding, and return to normal functioning.
fields.clarification_prompt: If repair differed by type of conflict, say so.

fields.label: How emotionally easy or settled did the relationship feel to you internally?
fields.placeholder: Low visible conflict does not automatically mean high internal ease.
fields.clarification_prompt: If ease changed with closeness or distance, say when.

fields.label: How much freedom did you have to remain yourself without feeling pressured to merge, reassure, or organize life around the relationship?
fields.placeholder: Focus on your experienced autonomy/engulfment.
fields.clarification_prompt: If cohabitation or attachment changed this, say how.

fields.label: How distressed were you by the possibility or reality of your partner having sex with somebody else?
fields.placeholder: Answer sexual jealousy only, not fear of losing romantic priority.
fields.clarification_prompt: If openness was acceptable, say so.

fields.label: How distressed were you by the possibility of your partner falling in love with or prioritizing somebody else romantically?
fields.placeholder: This can differ sharply from sexual jealousy.
fields.clarification_prompt: If the answer depended on how in love you were, say so.

fields.label: Did greater closeness, cohabitation, or attachment make pressure, conflict, or jealousy noticeably stronger?
fields.placeholder: Compare closer versus more distant phases.
fields.clarification_prompt: If there was no meaningful effect, say that.

RRQ_PRACTICAL_FUTURE.title: Practical future fit
RRQ_PRACTICAL_FUTURE.intro: Strong love can coexist with poor practical fit.

fields.label: How reliably did you support and care for each other's well-being in practice?
fields.placeholder: Think practical and emotional support, advocacy, and willingness to help.
fields.clarification_prompt: If support was asymmetric, say so.

fields.label: How well did your actual future plans fit?
fields.placeholder: Consider geography, money, work, family/children, religion, domestic life, relationship structure, lifestyle, and community.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name the domains that fit and the domains that did not.

fields.label: Which practical factors actually affected whether the relationship could continue?
fields.placeholder: Separate decisive practical factors from love, attraction, or sexual chemistry.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name what was decisive versus secondary.
